Fire HD 8 Tablet with Alexa, 8" HD Display, 16 GB, Black - with Special Offers (Previous Generation – 7th) Not too heavy, very handy. I got this for my mom who is 87 years old. She has always loved to read, but macular degeneration took that away from her until I got her the first Kindle and enlarged the print to about 2 words per page. She's been devouring books ever since, but the old Kindles didn't have that white background. I got her this one so she could read more than 2 words per page (now it's almost a sentence per page) and the lighted screen makes the print much brighter for her to see. The 8" is a comfortable size for her.

The learning curve has been a challenge. The screen is so sensitive that when she barely touches it, it loses her place. We have not tried Alexa to get her back to her place in her book, but we might try that and see if it works.

The promo info said it would hold a charge for 12 hours. Nope. We're doing good if it lasts 6 hours. I try to check it to make sure no other apps except Kindle are running, but it seems like the Internet is draining the battery... or something is. We've gone to turning it off completely so she can read a few hours before having to recharge.
text_fidelity_b: Fire HD 8 Tablet with Alexa, 8" HD Display, 16 GB, Black - with Special Offers (Previous Generation – 7th)

text_fidelity_a: Echo Dot (2nd Generation) - Smart speaker with Alexa - White This was purchased as a gift. I, the writer of this review, am the recipient of the gift. After about a year of "monkeying around" with this piece of technology, I have unplugged it and relegated it to a drawer. It simply doesn't work consistently. It often " has trouble connecting to the internet", even though nothing has changed. It often gets the voice commands wrong, or just doesn't respond. When it is working, (we use it mostly to stream music to a sound bar that I bought just to use with the dot by Blue tooth connection), it will often just quit, or pause and restart. I have had several conversations with the help desk at Amazon, and although very pleasant, the solution always seems to be the same. Turn it off and reinstall it. Not doing that any more. The WiFi is one room away, and lap tops, tablets and smart phones all work just fine in this room and others through out the house. It is sad, because this seemed like a great solution to get some music into this room without blasting it from several rooms away, but alas, it is a bust. Some of the things that it did, like the "this day in history" were fun, or the jokes she would tell were so silly that they were just funny, but that doesn't make the Dot worth the time, effort, or money. Save your money and buy a Blue tooth speaker for your phone. You'll be glad you did.

text_fidelity_a:
USB DAC Audio Converter Headphone Amplifier Type-C Port Digital to Analog Signal Audio Converter, 3.5MM Stereo Audio Optical Headphone Jack Output, Type-C Input Not to shabby of a gadget. It's just a wee little thing- fits in the palm of my hand- a little smaller than a deck of cards. Is powered through whatever device you are using. Does not need to be separately powered or charged.

What's in the (generic) box:
--Amplifier unit (roughly measured at 3.5" x 2.5" x .75")
--Type C to Type C Cable
--Type C to USB Cable
--3.5mm to 2rca Cable
--User Manual (a piece of paper with info)

I also received some other cable assembly in the box that I do not know what it is for. Appears to be used in Optical port. Bonus in terms of what is listed in product description, I guess.

What is on the Amplifier unit:
--One end of unit has: Headphone input, On/Off Switch for Bass, Volume knob
--Other end of unit has USB C port (in), Optical port (out), Gain (H/L) Switch, Line Out port.

Connection Diagram shows use between SPEAKERS OR HEADPHONES, and Mobile phone, Laptop, computer, or PS4. States that it does not work with tv. I haven't tried it yet, but I may attempt a work around- I'll let you know if I am successful.

In mean time, I have tried it between my smartphone (Pixel4XL) using AmazonMusic and two different types of speakers.

The first set of speakers is a nice plug in variety. They are circa 2004 CambridgeSoundWorks- where one cord is plugged into wall receptacle , and the other plug goes into a headphone port. They sound nice with use with my phone, so I didn't expect much difference when adding this amplifier. True enough, they have similar quality. My speakers without the amplifier are loud and I can hear some range. The addition of the amplifier allowed me to manipulate the bass, which can be nice depending on what I am listening to. I switched between High and Low on the gain switch. High boosts the overall sound, and low brings out a more mellow tone. Either are good.

Next, I tried it with a pair of novelty speakers circa 2002. Little SONYspeakers that are really just a headphone style output. So for purpose of review, using these is to mimic a set of basic headphones. They just happen to be in the shape of a speaker sitting on a desk rather than on the head. Cute little things, and when plugged into anything they really produce no further sound advantage over a basic set of headphones other than they aren't on the head. Thought these would be perfect to see how much this amplifier can help a bare bones basic sup par listening item. The sound went from a very low, just make out the music sound to truly being amplified. I could boost the volume and the sound opened up- not just got louder. So, while I will likely never use it with these, I thought hearing the difference on a terrible set of "speakers" (again, really just non head headphones) was absolutely worth mentioning. Tells me that this product IS working as intended.

Now, my Pixel4XL has fair sound already- not nuance, but not sounding like a tin can either. Using this with my nicer plug in speakers is great. Using my phone, with my nicer speakers AND this amplifier is a little nicer, but not hugely so. Perhaps in a larger room, or in other conditions where I may need a more dynamic sound to carry. This isn't a knock on the product, I think it is a nod toward the quality of my old speakers. I definitely can hear the improvement with ability to boost bass. High to high sounds similar. My speakers can't display a low end gain. So good for this product to offer that.

I do happen to have a speaker hooked up to my TV, and I am going to try to make that work if it doesn't complicate my wire management.

As for cord length.. if you are using it with your headphones, this is fine. You would otherwise be plugging it into the headphone port on your device, so really, with addition of the amplifier and the other cord to connect to device, you gain several extra inches of length. Beyond that, your mileage may vary in terms of what will work for you.

So far so good.

PS, I had low expectations of this unit, so I am impressed with my experience so far. As I continue to try it out with various devices in various environments, if I learn anything new-- good, bad, helpful, enlightening, I will surely be back to share.

I think it is worth trying out. I can't comment on price as I am not sure what these are really worth, and if there are true differences among the options out there. So my rating is based purely on effectiveness of product and accuracy of product description. If I had one wish on the options provided on this product, that would be to allow some additional range in the High/Low gain switch. HUANUO Dual Monitor Arm for 13 to 27 inch, Gas Spring Monitor Stands for 2 Monitors Vesa Mount with Clamp/Grommet Base, Computer Dual Monitor Desk Mount for up to 17.6 lbs per Arm At the current price tag, I am pretty amazed at these, considering the other type I have is (or more likely was) closer to $300. The other had a well-established brand name, although I don't actually remember what it was. They are actually pretty similar, with the other having decent instructions, feeling just slightly more solid, and better cable management overall.

They both have to be messed with, tightened, and tweaked to get them to work the way you want them to. Thankfully, I don't need either to be constantly moved, but constant re-positioning will be challenging on either stand. Both of them, you don't have to put a hole in your desk. You also need to be very careful (with both of them) to position your cables with just the right amount of slack so that they don't look stupid, but have enough slack to reposition when necessary without stretching the cables.

I like to use two small TVs to use as monitors and run 2 no-nonsense (i.e., thin) HDMI cables, coax, an audio cable, and the power to each. That way, you can set the desk up to accommodate two different docking stations. Don't forget Ethernet if the TVs are smart (mine are not, but they have PIP). If you really take your time, you can fit all that stuff in, and hopefully never have to re-run cables, because it is sort of a pain (but well worth it). Get black cables to match.

text_fidelity_a:
Seagate Backup Plus 2TB USB 3.0 Desktop External Hard Drive for Mac (STCB2000900) A solid backup drive is essential for anyone who requires a decent backup system, and sometimes a RAID is not an option. I took the 2TB option and while it's a good drive (so far) the cost difference between it and the 3TB drive makes it a less-than-ideal choice.

This drive is set up as an external server backup drive which stands on a desk. My primary concern was power - would this drive have its own power supply or would it rely on power through the USB port? As it turns out, it does have its own power supply which in my opinion is a very good thing.

I do not have a Mac so the first order of business was to format the drive for ext3 (Linux). This process took 4 hours over USB 2. That's a long time! That said, it's a big drive, and there were no errors in the process. It also confirmed something that was not clear on the packaging - this drive will work just fine with Linux, even though it is pre-formatted for Mac. In addition, this is a relatively quiet drive which is a pleasant bonus.

I have not had this drive very long but so far there have been no issues with it. It seems to be reliable and stable, and that's what is most important when using a drive for backups.

Seagate has put together a nice storage and backup drive with this drive. ALthough preformatted for Mac it can be reformatted for Windows or Linux file systems if desired.
text_fidelity_b: Seagate Backup Plus 2TB USB 3.0 Desktop External Hard Drive for Mac (STCB2000900)

text_fidelity_a:

I use these at work when I need to view videos without forcing my entire office to listen along and needed to find an alternative to my Apple ear pods because they always fall out of my ears.

I tested them out by listening higher fidelity version of my favorite Steely Dan songs and OMG I wasn't expecting this. These super cheap Panasonic ErgoFit In-Ear Earbud Headphones are fantastic and deliver big sound. I heard nuances in the music that I've never noticed before. The sound is balanced, and I even had to turn the volume down on my computer because they are very efficient (loud).

I am not an audiophile, but it sounded perfectly balanced to my ears. The bass isn't boomy, and the mid-range and highs are crystal clear. They sound better than our larger Sonos sound system. In fact, I needed to drown it out because my musical tastes differ widely from my crew.

The cord was plenty long, and I was able to comfortably reach the headphone jack from my desktop computer on the floor to my ears without it interfering or forcing me to sit in an awkward position while using them.

It came with multiple ear cushions to accommodate smaller ears, and I needed to use one of them for my right ear. I am super impressed with these and still cannot get over the price of these outstanding earbuds. Just buy them, you'll be more than happy!

text_fidelity_a:
Toshiba TY-CWU700 Vintage Style Retro Look Micro Component Wireless Bluetooth Audio Streaming & CD Player Wood Speaker System + Remote, USB Port for MP3 Playback, FM Stereo Digital Tuner, AUX Input This unit is large and not at all like the dimensions listed on Amazon. It is 5 inches high (top to bottom), 8 inches deep (front to back), and 16 inches in long (side-to-side).

WHAT COMES IN THE BOX:
- one speaker unit with both left and right speakers inside the large housing
- one power cord
- one FM antenna cord / wire
- one AAA battery
- one remote
- three user guides; one in English, Spanish, and French (I love this because I can keep the instructions in English and throw out the others)
- one limited 1-year warranty insert

FEATURES:
- Bluetooth speaker
- CD player
- FM Radio with ability for 30 preset radio stations
- Ability to operate controls via remote or front of the unit buttons
- Clock
- Sleep / timer function up to 120 minutes in 15-minute increments
- LED Dimmer
- USB terminal that supports USB memory (thumb drive) in FAT 16 or FAT 32 format
- Line In port to plug in an external audio device such as earphones / headphones

The sound this produces when I play my CDs was awesome and music to my ears. I also paired this speaker with my Google Nexus 7 Tablet (2013 version Android device) and my iPad Pro 12.9 and experienced moderately powerful sound there as well. The FM radio was staticky but that was due to the location of where I placed my unit. When I did receive a station, the sound was great.

In summary, this produces beautiful sound. As a Bluetooth speaker, it does not produce as powerful a sound as my [[ASIN:B00SNBCBBY ION Block Rocker]] but it is still good. The addition of the FM radio is a nice touch. I also like that it functions as an LED clock. The instructions and operation of the unit take a bit of getting use to and can be confusing but I was eventually able to figure it out; although I may have to consult the pamphlet every now and then. Overall, this is a well-rounded unit for indoor use but the unit is larger than I expected. It is as large as those old AM/FM amplifiers from years ago and has a retro 70’s look (see attached picture).

PS For those who are interested in comparisons, this is my sixth Bluetooth speaker. I ordered five other Bluetooth speakers over a several year period. I have a [[ASIN:B007ZG03DG Bose Wave Bluetooth Music Adapter]], which is not very good and a [[ASIN:B00MPMK3GW Goal Zero 94014 Rock Out 2 Green Solar Rechargeable Speaker]] which does not work when paired with some devices and, when it does pair well, it usually lacks the powerful sound I am looking for.

I also purchased one [[ASIN:B00SNBCBBY ION Audio Block Rocker (iPA76A) | Portable Bluetooth Speaker]] and one [[ASIN:B01N17AQ7U ION Audio IPA88 Tailgater Flash Wireless/Bluetooth Speaker]] both from Costco. I absolutely love the Block Rocker (except for when paired with my iPad Pro) and I only like the Tailgate Flash. The lights on the Tailgate Flash annoy me because they have to be turned off every time I power on the unit. Nevertheless, the sound from the ION speakers are usually awesome. The IONs are the only ones I use frequently indoors (even though they are more of an outdoor Bluetooth speaker). They are battery powered powerful speakers and the sound is intense. If one wants Bluetooth only with the capability of travelling with them without having to find a power outlet, then these are worth considering.

I also have a [[ASIN:B01MUG5WIN Sony XB20 Portable Wireless Speaker with Bluetooth, Blue (2017 model)]] which pairs well with my HP Omen Laptop and moderately well with my Nexus 7 and iPad Pro. However, this has to be charged first just like the Goal Zero speaker that I dislike.

PS My boyfriend connected his iPad 3 to this one's Bluetooth and loves it for listening to Podcasts. In order to get the volume as loud as he wanted, he also used the volume controls on the side of his iPad in conjunction with the volume knob on the Toshiba. On another note, he mentioned that the controls located below the CD player are very small for someone who has eye problems and I would agree with that. What I find inconvenient is that the button to open and close the CD player is there so that when the CD is open, I have to put my hand underneath it to close if I am not using the remote. Nevertheless, he loves this Toshiba just like I do.
text_fidelity_b: Toshiba TY-CWU700 Vintage Style Retro Look Micro Component Wireless Bluetooth Audio Streaming & CD Player Wood Speaker System + Remote, USB Port for MP3 Playback, FM Stereo Digital Tuner, AUX Input

Antennas Direct ClearStream 1MAX HDTV Antenna UHF VHF, Multi-Directional, 40+ Mile Range, UHD 4K, NEXTGEN TV – w/Adjustable Mounting Hardware (Black) Trying to decide if we were ready to cut the cord, we installed this antenna to see if we could get all the local channels. We got 40 digital channels about 20 miles west of Washington DC and the major networks are crystal clear.

The network towers we use are clustered together about 20 miles away. We have 2 or more topographical obstructions between our house and the towers (no line of sight). The Noise Margin on the networks is 35-40 dB. TVFool.com listed my location as "yellow" (which means use an attic antenna or higher). The cable drop is about 25 feet and I did not use an amplifier.

This antenna is supposed to be omni-directional but we did experience occasional signal drop on the networks with the initial "eyeball" installation (which was off about 15 degrees). Standing directly under the antenna and looking through a compass I had my son walk through the yard until he stepped into the path to the towers. Then I had him stand still, facing the antenna, and rotated it until he told me it was pointed straight over his head. That seemed to fix the signal drops. Given all the factors of our situation, I am probably maxing out the performance of this antenna. If I have any issues I'll just buy the add-on the reflector shield to increase directional performance...but for right now I don't need it.

Installation was easy (I just mounted it to the Direct TV mast). This antenna is small and light which was a big plus when climbing up a 25 foot ladder.

So far so good!
text_fidelity_b: Antennas Direct ClearStream 1MAX HDTV Antenna UHF VHF, Multi-Directional, 40+ Mile Range, UHD 4K, NEXTGEN TV – w/Adjustable Mounting Hardware (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
NETGEAR Orbi Pro WiFi 6 Tri-Band Mesh System (SXK50), Router with 1 Satellite Extender for Business or Home, VLAN, QoS, Coverage up to 5,000 sq. ft, 75 Devices, AX5400 802.11 AX (up to 5.4Gbps) The rise of home automation devices means that many of us have a lot more devices that connect to our wifi networks. While most of those devices use the 2.4Ghz frequency while devices like phones, tablets, and firetv use 5Ghz to stay out of each other's way, it still means that there are so many more devices to manage in a network and all of them are attempting to talk on the network. Not to mention interference from neighbors and their many devices.

This drives the need for beefy routers with faster CPUs to manage all of the chatter and radios that allow many more simultaneously connected devices.

The NETGEAR Orbi Pro WiFi 6 Tri-band Mesh System (SXK80) attempts to address these needs. Sporting the latest wireless Wifi 6 technology, most of the basic features that a router needs (QoS, DDNS, VPN), and 60+ device support, the SKX80 holds a lot of promise.

Unlike one of the upvoted reviews, I don't have a different AX system to compare this to so for me, this mesh router performs admirably. It is fast and has good coverage. In my time so far, I haven't had any dropped connections. Videos stream well and web browsing works fine. I don't normally do voice or video calls while walking around the house, but watching videos while walking seem to work well. My device will jump from router to satellite correctly and there is no disruption to the video playback.
text_fidelity_b: NETGEAR Orbi Pro WiFi 6 Tri-Band Mesh System (SXK50), Router with 1 Satellite Extender for Business or Home, VLAN, QoS, Coverage up to 5,000 sq. ft, 75 Devices, AX5400 802.11 AX (up to 5.4Gbps)

Inventiv Sport Wireless Bluetooth Audio Sunglasses, Open Ear Headphones Music & Hands-Free Calling, for Men & Women, Polarized Glasses Lenses (Black Frame/Blue Tint) I like to listen to audio books as I go on bike rides, so I've been looking for a product like this. When I run I use over the ear headphones, but I can't fit those on over or under my cycling helmet. These sunglasses are a great solution. There are speakers underneath the arms that broadcast music almost directly into your ears. The effect is an open ear speaker system that allows you to hear your music, but also lets you stay mindful of ambient noises.

The sunglasses have enough of a tint to be comfortable, but not so much that they are impractical in low light. The arms rest easily on your ears and the nose piece is a solid bit of plastic that does not pinch the bridge of your nose. The glasses are very light even with the battery and speaker system.

The sunglasses connect to your cell phone via Bluetooth without any issues. There is a large power button on the right arm that is easy to locate by touch. I preferred these for comfort and for sound quality to ear buds. The sound quality is about what you'd expect for tiny speakers mounted to the arms of sunglasses. It's not concert hall quality, but it gets the job done, and it's better than a lot of other speakers on the market.

These sunglasses are great for athletes who like to listen to music while they're out exercising. Also included is a case, a bag, a lens cloth, and a charging cable.

text_fidelity_a: WYZE Cam 1080p HD Indoor Smart Home Camera with Night Vision, 2-Way Audio, Compatible with Alexa & the Google Assistant Bulbs and outlet are OK. I would not buy separately though, as nowadays you get higher quality bulbs and outlets for a discount price.  The sensor bridge, contact and motion sensors are problematic to say the least. I have 2 contact sensors and 3 motion sensors connected to the sensor bridge. Right now all of them are offline, they started going offline one by one. Distance from the sensors to the bridge is not an issue since two of them are located no more than three feet away from the bridge. This is not the first time this has happened. The only solution for me has been to reset bridge and sensors, and reinstall them one by one. Many people complain about the same issue, and this keeps happening. The camera where the bridge is attached is installed 7 ft from the ground, so it has been very aggravating to have to get a ladder every time one of these switches has gone offline. Regarding the camera, you probably will not find anything cheaper in the market right now. This model in particular offers continuous recording provided you insert a storage card, that is a plus. Person detection is back, however sometimes it takes more than 10 minutes to receive a notification. Some people has reported that it has take up to one hour to get the notification. I personally would not recommend getting this package due to the unreliability of the bridge and motion and contact sensors. This is definitely not a system you want to buy to secure your home. The camera can be purchased separately for about $25. The video quality is acceptable during the daytime. If you want a hobby camera, you will not find a better deal. For security purposes, you are better off looking somewhere else.
text_fidelity_b: WYZE Cam 1080p HD Indoor Smart Home Camera with Night Vision, 2-Way Audio, Compatible with Alexa & the Google Assistant

We got another one listed at $40 and besides for the branding, it seems to be the same binocular with slight molding differences. The tech is the same. Don't bother spending a little more unless you really want to upgrade and get one with zoom function. All these economy versions do not have zoom. And if you're new to binoculars, there is a learning curve, but this is how you focus:

1. Set the RIGHT EYEPIECE dial to ZERO and set sight on a distant subject. I'm not sure what zero means since there are no numbers, but there are arrows, so I presume it's when the arrows line up.

2. Cover the RIGHT FRONT lens with your hand, and rotate the FOCUSING WHEEL (the middle wheel), until the image is sharp. Keep both eyes open while you make this adjustment.

3. Now cover the LEFT FRONT lens and rotate the RIGHT EYEPIECE dial until the image is sharp. So here, you're not touching the focusing wheel, you're adjusting the RIGHT EYEPIECE dial.

text_fidelity_a:
(OLD MODEL) Seagate Expansion 3TB Desktop External Hard Drive USB 3.0 (STBV3000100) So far, the hard drive is working as one would expect. As always with these things, the questions mostly arise in longevity/reliability issues, so I'll be updating this once I've had a longer time to determine how it does in those categories. First impressions at this point, though:

1) the drive has a relatively small footprint, which is nice

2) Feels quite sturdy and hefty (it's surprisingly heavy) with good build quality

3) This isn't powered by your USB, so you'll need an outlet for its enclosed power cord

4) When you start up, it takes a little while (a few seconds) for the display light to come on. At first, I thought it hadn't started up at all, but just wait a small bit and it will light up

5) the display light is located on top but at the rear of the device, which while minor, is a slight inconvenience. I have it under my desk set back a little ways, so to see the light isn't as immediate as one might like

6) the drive is quite quiet. Not silent--you can hear it--but definitely quieter than many I've had

7) the drive is pretty fast, with the uptick from USB 2 to 3 very noticeable as I move from one computer (USB 2) to the other (USB 3)--it varies depending on what I'm copying, but sometimes the difference is half the speed

8) despite the small footprint, with its necessity for power and it's weight, I wouldn't consider this at all a portable drive, though I suppose you could use it as such. But really, it's big and heavy for that.

9) I use this on several Macs--no problem at all reformatting it for those computers--just a few mouse clicks and a few seconds is all

So far, this is a good big backup drive (I have the 5 TB version). And since we all know, or should, that drives will fail, you can't have too many of them. If any issues arise over time, I'll update accordingly
text_fidelity_b: (OLD MODEL) Seagate Expansion 3TB Desktop External Hard Drive USB 3.0 (STBV3000100)

text_fidelity_a:
Fire Tablet with Alexa, 7" Display, 16 GB, Blue - with Special Offers (Previous Generation - 5th) Let's begin with the cons:
This is NOT an Android tablet, even tho it looks like it. You CAN NOT download apps from the Google Play Store (at least, not without jumping through some hoops), the apps available on the Amazon Apps are sorely lacking in some areas (many of the apps I use and really like on Google Play are not available), the OS is slow and clumsy, the home screen is not particularly user friendly and the HOME button is only accessed through a screen, not a dedicated button, which makes it a pain in the butt (sometimes, not always.)
Now, for the pros:

text_fidelity_a:
Monoprice Blackbird 4K 3x1 HDMI 1.4 Switch - Compact, HDCP 2.2, Built-in Equalizer, 4K 30Hz, YCbCr 4:4:4, 18Gbps (Compatible with PS4/5 Xbox Apple TV Fire Stick Roku Blu-Ray Player) Since we mounted our TV we like to use as few chords as possible. This way they are neatly tucked along the wall and down into the entertainment center where all our entertainment equipment is housed. So the main HDMI cable runs down but of course we have more components that require a cable than the one connected to the TV. Our solution? A signal splitter. Thankfully, we have only three output connections so this one seemed perfect. Plus, it touts 4k signal, even though most pre-4k HDMI boxes should be fine, but it's nice to have that in the title just in case.

What I use this mostly for is the cable box and a couple of video game systems. As for the cable box, seems to work fine; no dropped signals that I've noticed, nor any degradation in quality. As for game consoles, I have the PS3 and the Wii U hooked up to it. SAme: no noticeable quality degradation nor input lag.
Now, to put it to the real test, I hooked up some retro consoles that have been modded to output native HDMI; that means they'll be HDMI with no lag. Considering I have this and two HDMI cables connecting the console to the TV, I was curious to see if there truly was any lag.
With older games, timing is everything, especially on the 8-bit consoles with platformers and fighters, like the NES. From what I could tell, there was absolutely no lag, not to mention signal loss. The buttons responded as though I were using a normal NES on a CRT.

So yeah, I'm pretty satisfied. It's a bit light and doesn't have heavy pads on the bottom to prevent it from sliding around. With so many cables, and the ability to use the remote control, it should be a bit more stable on the surface.
I haven't used the remote as the detections are instant. No need to manually switch the inputs, at least from my experience. Also, I didn't need to use the power adapter; the power from the HDMI cables seemed to be sufficient, and the detection was not complicated by the lack of adapter. Weird.
text_fidelity_b: Monoprice Blackbird 4K 3x1 HDMI 1.4 Switch - Compact, HDCP 2.2, Built-in Equalizer, 4K 30Hz, YCbCr 4:4:4, 18Gbps (Compatible with PS4/5 Xbox Apple TV Fire Stick Roku Blu-Ray Player)

text_fidelity_a:
Lenovo Legion Y720 Gaming Laptop, 15.6" Full HD, Intel Core i7-7700HQ Processor, 16GB DDR4 RAM, 512GB SSD, GeForce GTX 1060-6GB, Windows 10 Signature Image - 80VR0078US Like all dedicated gaming laptops, this is a big heavy high-powered machine. It is portable enough to lug over to your buddy's house for play dates, but it is too bulky and heavy to carry to work everyday. Construction is very good with an aggressive-looking aluminum case to match the aggressive-sounding "Legion" product name. Mechanical keyboard has decent (but not the best) travel and the large keys are backlit so you can easily play your games in the dark. Dolby Atmos audio works well for games, but is kind of thin for music or movies unless you hook it up to external speakers. This Y720 version has a 1080p IPS display, which is OK but not as bright or contrasty as some other laptops I have used. There is also a more expensive 4K display available, but I have not tried that.

Core i7 CPU with 16GB of RAm gives you really great performance. This machine is easily powerful enough for any games I tried on it. Even though performance is throttled somewhat when run off the battery, battery life is still less than 2 hours under heavy use (maybe 6 hours with light use).

For the money, it is hard to go wrong with these Lenovo Legions. If you don't want to spend more than $1000, the cheaper Legion Y520 is almost as good for most types of games and costs $300 less.
text_fidelity_b: Lenovo Legion Y720 Gaming Laptop, 15.6" Full HD, Intel Core i7-7700HQ Processor, 16GB DDR4 RAM, 512GB SSD, GeForce GTX 1060-6GB, Windows 10 Signature Image - 80VR0078US

text_fidelity_a:
Fantom GreenDrive 500 GB USB 2.0/eSATA Desktop External Hard Drive with 2 Year Warranty GD500EU Firstly, let me say that, being a closet tech-geek. I have owned countless hard drives over the last two decades. I own stock in Seagate, so I purchased [[ASIN:B000ND75C0 Seagate FreeAgent 500 GB 3.5-Inch USB 2.0 Hard Drive ST305004FDA1E1-RK]], (only the 1TB version) from them and, to my dismay, it just stopped responding to power after a couple of months (I got it working, but it was a let-down for sure with the stock thing and all). Then, I ordered this really, really expensive, crappy paperweight here: [[ASIN:B006Y5UV4A WD My Passport 1TB Portable External Hard Drive Storage USB 3.0 Black]] (same basic drive, just an earlier model no longer offered, I think), and was ready to use it for skeet practice in no time. I hated that I needed to use their software to access the data on the drive. As for the actual software, it was a total PITA. But it didn't matter because, within weeks, the damned thing crashed for good--and I wasn't even doing anything weird with it. :|

So, about three years ago, I stumbled upon the Fantom Greendrive and was, at first, kind of put-off by the apparent size (it's actually not as big as the Seagate, it turns out). I really wanted something small and portable. But, after all those issues with other drives, I really, REALLY wanted something RELIABLE. I first did some research, took a chance and ordered this drive.

DEAR GOD. IT IS MARVELOUS.

That was, as I've said, three years ago. Three years of constant use: heavy data transfer, being knocked around (even dropped on the ground a couple of times), never defragged (I got lazy cos' it's so reliable), never disk-checked, numerous power-loss and disconnection incidents....nothing can kill it! It hums along nicely no matter what you throw its way.

You don't have to ever worry about unmounting it before you turn off the power--you just unplug it and go. It's never failed me and, to be honest, that makes it better than one particular husband, in my book (the second is doing quite nicely, thank you).

The "Green" is for:

---Firstly, it doesn't take a lot of power. Nice.

---Secondly, despite being dropped a few times, it hums nicely and quietly. No loud grinding at all. I always have to check to see if it's on (which is easy because a green light shines through the grate of the front to let you know the power is on).

---Thirdly, if you have it plugged in but haven't accessed it in a while (like fifteen minutes), it will initiate a semi-hibernation, then go into a bit of a deeper hibernation after like a half hour or so (never timed it, but it's cool when it does it). So if you hear a click and a sound like the motor is clicking off, that's what you're hearing. Cooler still, the minute you click to access the drive it's ready to go--little to no wait.

It's also very fast. As drives go, mine is almost full and THREE YEARS OLD and, like I said, never defragged, yet it still runs faster for data transfer than my brand new laptop...which makes me wonder about my laptop. ;/

I actually love this drive so much, I figured with my bad luck, one day it's finally going to give up on me and quit for good. So, about a year ago I purchased the newer 2TB drive[[ASIN:B002XITVCA Micronet Technology Fantom GreenDrive 2 TB USB 2.0/eSATA Desktop External Hard Drive GD2000EUS]]for more space and extra backup. I love having the two of them because, unlike many products, Fantom keeps the peripherals consistent, so the power supplies (though upgraded to a one-piece rather than two-piece on the newer model) are interchangeable, as are the USB cables (though the 2TB, being newer, is obviously a 3.0 rather than a 2.0). Still, transferring data between the two is easy-cheesy and fast.

So, all in all, I have to tell you that, despite being an incurable tech-geek, this drive is honestly the best, most reliable, and durable piece of electronics equipment I've EVER owned.
text_fidelity_b: Fantom GreenDrive 500 GB USB 2.0/eSATA Desktop External Hard Drive with 2 Year Warranty GD500EU

text_fidelity_a:
Cooler Master Hyper 212 EVO V2 CPU Air Cooler with SickleFlow 120, PWM Fan, Direct Contact Technology, 4 Copper Heat Pipes for AMD Ryzen/Intel LGA1700/1200/1151, Silver/Black I have had this CPU fan now going on 5 months. I love this fan. I hadn't upgraded for nearly 10 years and decided on an AMD FM2 Black Edition 6300 6-core CPU with an MSI 970A-G43 Plus economy Micro Board and 16GB of Corsair Memory 4GBx4 in the 4 slots. I use my computer for gaming and all around use. I wanted a CPU cooler that would be quiet and still keep my cpu cool when I cranked it up for high-performance gaming. I found it with this AND it didn't break the bank. With the Turbo Clock OC setting it will idle down and bolt up to 4300mhz seamlessly while the fan moves from it's WHISPER silent 36c idle and general use, to it's 42c full bore o'clocked gaming use. The fan keeps it cool, and never does the fan become obtrusive or loud.

This fan is BIG. Don't even consider it if you have a micro or small mid-tower case. Your case must be generous in it's width to accommodate this cooler. Be sure to check the dimensions of your case with the unit. I have an older Antec 900 case it fit snugly into. I did have to remove the optional side window cooler intake fan I had installed with the prev board, cpu and cooler to allow it's fit. Also be sure your motherboard design placement of Memory slots is such that your Memory will clear it. My board's Corsair Vengence Memory JUST cleared it by a couple mm's laterally, and the top of the memory overtakes the bottom edge of cooler by about a quarter inch. If you are in the process of building your system a choice with low profile memory that doesn't have the tall heat spreaders would be a wise choice and safe bet if you are unsure about clearance with a board design that puts the memory slots very close to the CPU and cooler position. In the first photo attached I REVERSED the fan position to PULL the air thru on Left for best clearance instead of PUSHING the air through on the right if you just don't have the room, that flexibility is very handy. I wasn't satisfied with the cooling level and re-positioned the fan on right to PUSH it through later on and it sent the temps down a few more degrees. As you can see though in the second photo, it is much more snug.

Bottom line, a great cooler IF your case and build offers the room to fit it in. I would recommend it for those wanting great overclocking cooling performance and very quiet operation. I think most overclock enthusiasts would be well served to try this value priced solution before expensive and complicated water cooled solutions.
text_fidelity_b: Cooler Master Hyper 212 EVO V2 CPU Air Cooler with SickleFlow 120, PWM Fan, Direct Contact Technology, 4 Copper Heat Pipes for AMD Ryzen/Intel LGA1700/1200/1151, Silver/Black

text_fidelity_a:
Blink Outdoor Camera Wall Mount Bracket, Hard Protective Case and Metal Mount for Blink XT2 Cameras Weather Proof Adjustable Indoor Outdoor Mount and Cover for Blink Home Security(3 Pack, Black) When I installed my Blink XT2, I found I needed to move it a little lower so I could maybe see the face of the delivery person. Thinking I could unscrew the mount without removing the camera, I turned the camera to one side so I could access the screws. The camera fell to the floor. A little bit of friction is not sufficient to hold these cameras. That is when I started looking at these mounts which SHOULD be included in the box.

This is in several parts. Plastic camera-enclosing parts are held together with 4 small screws. The metal part is attached to the wall with 3 flat-head #6 screws.

Unscrew the adjusting part so the base of the mount can be attached to the wall. Do not try to adjust the angle unless this part is loose. Use care when tightening the screws - do it manually so the screws are not over-tightened. The aluminum base could be cracked by over-tightening.

The small screws that are used to attach the back cover to the front should be machine screws, and the posts into which they are screwed should be metal. This is my opinion and is because these screws will have to be removed and reinstalled every time the batteries are replaced.

One piece of plastic had a small 'tab' on it that had to be cut off before the back cover would attach to the front.

A hole in the bottom of the plastic is there to allow a charging cable to be attached. If you do not plan to use rechargeable batteries and have no need for the USB cable, plug the hole so insects do not go inside looking for a new home. I used a small piece of closed cell foam packing material (photo).

If you want to use these mounts with the earlier Blink cameras, you might want to use some foam so the camera does not move around inside the enclosure (photo).
text_fidelity_b: Blink Outdoor Camera Wall Mount Bracket, Hard Protective Case and Metal Mount for Blink XT2 Cameras Weather Proof Adjustable Indoor Outdoor Mount and Cover for Blink Home Security(3 Pack, Black)

I have it next to my computer that I use to listen to Amazon streaming MP3 music. My main speakers are NHT Model Twos, and this subwoofer supplies an excellent bottom end to the music. I haven't played it loud yet, but I'm looking forward to trying it out on a movie soundtrack.

The power switch has three positions -- Off, On, and Auto. In the Auto setting, it turns itself on if it senses an incoming signal. When I'm playing music softly, I'm finding that it takes a while to discover that it should turn on. In my case, the subwoofer is sitting next to my desk, and it's not hard to reach the power switch. But keep this in mind if you want to hide it somewhere that would make the power switch hard to reach. (It's near the top of the rear of the cabinet.) There's also a phase switch, with two positions. There's no magic to that; just set it to the position that sounds best. As with all subwoofers, the placement in your room isn't critical, although the subwoofer's sound can be somewhat amplified if you locate it in a corner.

Update: I've had time now to use this with lots of different types of music, as well as TV and movies. The bass is very solid and tight, with no boominess at all. It blends beautifully, with plenty of power for my medium-sized room. This is very musical, adding firm support that's more than just "punch". This is surely one of the best values in powered subwoofers, and I'd buy it again in a heartbeat.

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Keyboard 3G, Free 3G + Wi-Fi, 6" E Ink Display - includes Special Offers & Sponsored Screensavers This is by far the best ereader on the market.

The bad.

It doesn't do epub and it doesn't connect to the library. This seems like a deal breaker until you try to borrow a book from the library. I have one on hold now (to read on either the nook or the Sony) that should be available in 39 weeks. I'll probably give up and just buy it anyway.

The good.

The speed. The page turns are as fast as the average person can turn a print page. You won't see that "opening book" message the nook displays. When you tell it to open a book, it opens in less than a second. I keep hitting the page turn key just to marvel at how fast it is. I've never seen an ereader this fast. This is perfect.

Store access. Let me run you through buying a book for the various devices. For the Kindle, if you're on the Amazon site you select your book, click buy now, pick up the device and start reading. For the nook, you buy the book, then you turn on the touch screen that keeps turning itself off, you go into the home screen, go to "My Library", select "Update B&N Content" and wait a few minutes. There is no mechanism to automatically push content to the device. For the Sony (I'm using the Daily Edition, which has 3G), you use the custom software (no way to buy from a website), buy the book, then either transfer it via USB, or go to the device, to the store, log into your account (you need to provide your login information each time you go to the store) find the book you bought and click download, then wait. For buying from the device, Kindle is easy and fast, nook is decent, and Sony is unreasonably slow.

The screen. There is no glare, even with the book light on. It's the crispest and easiest to read screen out there. It's beautiful.

Audible integration. Download your books via WiFi or transfer via USB and listen with your device, either through headphones or the speakers. How cool is that? Now if only there were a card reader to store those larger files.

Collections. I have the Kindle 1, so I was first introduced to collections via Sony. It's great to be able to organize so much content. Here you can organize ebooks and audiobooks into collections together. That's one thing Kindle and Sony both have over nook--they treat content the same. Nook is the only one that doesn't let you annotate or bookmark newspapers and magazines, and who wouldn't want to mark an article to refer back to later?

Ease of use. I handed my Kindle 1 to a woman who was too scared of technology to turn on her own laptop. Her husband had to do it for her. I wanted to show her a passage in the Declaration of Independence, and I had the passage on the screen. I didn't instruct her. Moments later, she turned the page and just kept reading, all the way the end. Then she looked at what else I had on the device. An ereader should be as easy and intuitive to use as a print book, and most of us figured those out when we were about 10 months old. Kindle fits that bill.

Social networking. Post passages and comments on them to Twitter and Facebook. You can see what passages other readers have highlighted. This is particularly great for online book clubs.

More language sets. I'm kind of hoping Amazon will sell Japanese language books in the US Kindle store, or let us buy from Amazon.co.jp.

I could go on and on, but what it comes down to is, when it comes down to the core features of an ereader--buying, reading, annotating, and searching a book, Kindle beats the competition hands down. When it comes to extra bells and whistles--organization, commenting to others, web access, text to speech, Kindle beats the competition hands down.

There is no other viable choice any more. Kindle is just too much better than every other device out there.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Keyboard 3G, Free 3G + Wi-Fi, 6" E Ink Display - includes Special Offers & Sponsored Screensavers

I haven't tried to see if it is eligible, but I assume it would not be. As of this writing (10/12/2014), that vendor, CD Supply, is still offering the lens - though now for $170. Still an incredible deal for this lens which came new in the standard Canon box with manual etc. (If it isn't warranteed - I can buy another and still be about the price of just one at regular price).

The lens itself: I was pleasantly surprised. I could have purchased it in my kit with the 70D camera, but wasn't really interested. For $140 - what the heck. The photos are sharper than from the kit 18-135mm STM IS lens in my opinion (and that's a pretty decent lens as kit lenses go). It is very small and light weight for a pretty long lens - especially on a crop sensor.
BONUS: Macro. It actually can get pretty decent magnification. Something like 1/4:1 from a pretty good distance at 250mm.
Plus it works great with extension tubes. I've used it with 12mm and 26mm (not together) and it worked great. Even autofocus - though I wouldn't recommend that for Macro.

Negatives (though - again - if you get it for cheap, these are quibbles):
- No lens hood provided. Buy a knock off on Amazon for $13
- Not a super bright lens. You're going to need some decent sunlight or a good flash with this. It ramps up to f/5 minimum pretty quick and f/5.6 not too long after that. Only the widest shots will get F/4.
- Pretty cheaply built (but it's a cheap lens!)

Can you tell I'm excited? Anytime I can boost my entertainment for less dollars is always a good day. The Roku will pay for itself in 2 months after switching to basic. And its HD!

Sigh...I must go.

I've been watching the original Dr. Who from the 60's.

What makes this cable really exceptional are the connector ports. TCL 65" Class 4-Series 4K UHD HDR Roku 2017 Smart TV - 65S405 Do not be afraid! This is a great TV.

The good: I won't go into the technical details and explanations. Others have done that for me. We purchased this for a new home and have had it set up for a couple of weeks. The integration of Roku is seamless, and it retains those same intuitive menus. It has no WiFi connectivity issues for us (we have a Google mesh network with a good signal at the TV location), and effortlessly streams Netflix, Amazon Video and You TubeTV-- DVR and live-- and looks great doing it. I haven't tried 4K content yet, so can't comment on that.

The bad: It doesn't handle low light scenes very well in movies and television, and particularly when viewed from any angle that isn't straight on. That's why I gave it four stars instead of five. If you can overcome that, forge ahead! I couldn't justify spending twice or more on Samsung or others. Another minor quibble-- silver feet on a black frame looks a little odd.

text_fidelity_a:
Corsair Vengeance 2000 Wireless 7.1 Gaming Headset (CA-9011115-NA) For the price, this is a decent set of gaming headphones. The build quality is perfectly fine for the price point. It doesn't feel as rock solid as more expensive brands, but feels like it will certainly stand up to normal usage.

The comfort is borderline. It feels fine for up to about an hour of usage, then the ear cups start to become somewhat uncomfortable and the headband pinches a bit. It's not the best set for hours and hours of usage, but for "normal" wear times I didn't have any problems.

The sound quality is quite good. Nice amount of bass response without sounding muddy. I also found it to have more than good enough sound quality for watching movies, with the dialogue coming through clearly. It's not the best for listening to music (the mid and upper ranges are a bit constrained) but for it's intended purpose of a gaming set, no complaints at all regarding sound quality.

My major problem was with range. I love the fact that these are wireless, but placement is critical. I'd lose the signal if I didn't vary much from a specific spot near the wireless adapter. Moving just a bit out of the "zone" killed the connection. That was a disappointment since, while I didn't expect to be able to roam around the house with them on, I did expect to be able to leave my chair and go a short distance without breaking the connection. No problems with signal strength when seated or within a few feet of the adapter, but hit and miss when moving more than a few feet away.

Other than the range issue, this is a pretty good value in a gaming headphone set.
text_fidelity_b: Corsair Vengeance 2000 Wireless 7.1 Gaming Headset (CA-9011115-NA)

iPad Stand TechMatte Multi-Angle Aluminum Holder for Tablets, E-Readers and Smartphones, Nintendo Switch - Mini Stand The heft of this stand is impressive. I was expecting a lightweight stand, but was really surprised at how heavy and solid it was when I took it out of the box. It's the type of stand that I get the impression that I could run over with my car and not damage it. The hinge and the "kick stand" portion are made of plastic, but they also feel substantial.

The angle is set by depressing a button in the hinge area. It's very easy to adjust, and the hinge has click stops at various angles that hold it securely.

What is not adjustable is the depth of the cutout that holds the tablet or phone. I didn't have any problems with it holding a variety of tablets (iPad, Kindle and Nexus). It won't, however, hold some tablets that have a skin on it. The cutout that holds the table is slanted, and is 10mm at the widest point at the top, and 8mm at the narrowest point at the bottom. You'll want to measure your tablet plus skin to make sure it fits.

The cutout for the tablet has a plastic non-skid insert that works well. The stand itself also has plastic nubs on the back to prevent scratches on the tablet, and nubs on the bottom to prevent scratches on the table top. The nubs also act as non-skid points.

Very solid build quality, very easy to adjust in a variety of angles, and the design ensures that there won't be any damage to the tablet when you take if off/put it on the stand. As long as the width does not present a problem, this is a great choice for a tablet stand. Highly recommend.

text_fidelity_a:
Moshi iVisor XT (HD clear) No-Bubble Screen Protector for the Fire HDX 8.9" I purchased this protector due to the overwhelming positive reports from other verified buyers. I do not like my cell phone's screen being unprotected and now with my first Kindle I feel the same way. The HDX screen is gorgeous and I want a way to keep it as such. This screen protector seemed the answer to my predicament.

This protector is, indeed, extremely simple to 'install'. It takes more time to remove it from its packaging and throw the trash away afterwards than it does to apply the protector itself. Simply line up the cutouts on the protector film with the camera and flash at the top and center of your Kindle and you are done. I found it helpful to guide the film into place by kind of rolling the sides down, guiding them to ensure proper placement. Then just apply a little pressure (basically, run your hand around the edges) to activate the adhesive.

Only the outer black margin of the protector has adhesive to stick it to the border and outer edges of your Kindle, thus leaving the clear center which covers your Kindle's screen loose, or non-sticky. This manufacturing and design approach has both pros and one con I have noticed so far.

Pros:

It allows for lightning fast and super easy installation.

Because of the solid black border, you can accidentally touch the sticky side while installing and lining it up without any fingerprints showing through as with a normal screen protector. This was a bonus to me as these things are always so difficult to install without this happening.

The clear center portion that covers the screen is completely 100% bubble free.

Due to some micro hairs/fibers being on the screen despite having wiped it down prior to installing the protector, I learned that I could remove the protector (lifted up one corner and peeled it halfway back to do a quick swipe with the MF cloth again) and it would re-adhere to the Kindle's surface just as well as it did the first time.

The company claims that, if it should lose its stickiness, the protector can be rinsed/washed and used again. I have yet to need to go this far so I cannot comment on the credit-worthiness of this claim, however from my experiences so far, I can see the possibility of this claim holding up.

I have not noticed any blurring or the rainbow affect the company mentions on its packaging. The screen is crystal clear and appears to not even have a screen protector on it.

Con:

Since the clear center portion does not adhere to the screen, it is allowed to float just above the screen thus reducing the screen sensitivity and requiring more force from either your fingertip or your stylus.

After using my Kindle for a few hours after installation of this screen protector, I have come to the above conclusions. As bad as the con is for me and my preferences, I will leave it on for a few days to give myself a little more time and to see if anything changes. This screen protector ranks very high on my list of desirable protectors (I even searched to see if they make a version for my Droid cell phone) so I am really hoping that the sensitivity issue works itself out soon.
text_fidelity_b: Moshi iVisor XT (HD clear) No-Bubble Screen Protector for the Fire HDX 8.9"

Silverstone Tek Professional Slim 120mm Fan with Fine-Tuned Performance and Low Noise Cooling FN123 My custom wooden PC case was running a bit hot (around 48* C at idle with a Pentium G3220), so I had two options. Option 1 was to buy this fan and create a recess in the lid of my case to mount it (the reason I chose this slim fan over a more powerful 25mm thick fan). Option 2 was to shell out three or four times what this fan costs for a slim CPU cooler (my case is quite small) and hope that it works better than the stock Intel cooler.

I went with the more budget friendly Option 1, took the time to create the 15mm recess, and am happy to report that my idle temp dropped 15* (33* C vs 48) and after half an hour of CPU torture with Prime95, it was holding steady at 60* C (still 12* shy of the max temp for this CPU). I have the fan mounted horizontally (not ideal for a sleeve bearing fan like this, I know) and while I understand that my use case isn't typical, I'm quite happy with my purchase.

If anything changes, I'll update my review accordingly.
text_fidelity_b: Silverstone Tek Professional Slim 120mm Fan with Fine-Tuned Performance and Low Noise Cooling FN123

text_fidelity_a:
Kinivo BTC450 Bluetooth Car Kit (Hands-Free Adapter for Cars with 3.5mm Aux Input, Apt-X) I'm very satisfied with this product. The auto-connect feature is my favorite part. I can leave my phone in my pocket, never having taken it out and still listen to my music on my iPhone (where it left off) and take/make phone calls as well. Very easy to pair my phone with the device. When my car turns off, the device is disengaged and disconnects from my phone. When I turn my car on, it takes about 3 seconds and then I hear a small beep noise, and now I can click the button on the puck which resumes my music/media.

Like my title says, this is exactly what I wanted. I wanted complete hands-free in my car, but didn't want to use any annoying bluetooth earpieces. The sound quality is good as well. I did get some loop noise in my 2008 Mazda 3 so I did have to buy a female-to-female 3.5 mm part from RadioShack for $5 which resolved the noise problem. I already had a cable with a noise loop shield so all I needed was this part. You can also buy little filter clamps at RadioShack which you would just place right on the cable and should reduce noise. The part was only $3, I just chose to use my existing part instead which I also bought on Amazon
([[ASIN:B0031U1ATQ Kensington Reducing SmartPhone including iPhone]]

Overall, 5 stars! Great product! The price is right. I'm a happy customer. It was shipped and received sooner than I expected. I am overjoyed about this product.

text_fidelity_a:
Amazon Basics 3-Button Wired USB Computer Mouse, Black - Pack of 30 I read over the reviews here and I'm here to tell you that if I can pay less than $10 for a mouse, I will not complain if it only lasts a year. Or even six months. I've spent upwards of $50 on computer mice that have lasted for fewer months.

All that said, there is one reason I bought it. Amazon stands behind it and it is BASIC. That is all I needed. This isn't for gaming, so no need to spend all that money. I use it for word processing and editing. I use it for online activities. Nothing crucial and nothing that is heavy use. My hand doesn't stay on it, so whether it is ergonomic or not, really doesn't matter to me. I type, then I stop and use the mouse, then I type again. You should always, when purchasing online, read everything carefully, then consider how you will use the item. If you have a large hand, this mouse probably will not be comfortable for you to use constantly. It is small. But then, the description tells you that. If you are looking for a mouse that is functional, doesn't cost a lot, you aren't using it for gaming, and you can lighten your touch, then this is for you. It isn't going to withstand rough usage. This is perfect for me and a lot of other users.
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Basics 3-Button Wired USB Computer Mouse, Black - Pack of 30

text_fidelity_a:
JVC HAECX20B Sports Clip Inner Ear Headphones, Black The sound quality of these earbuds AKA headphones is excellent. They are exactly what they are advertised to be, earbuds with clips that go over the ears to keep them from falling out of your ears when you are engaged in activities that cause a lot of moving and shaking of your head, which would dislodge ordinary earbuds.

I don't personally engage in sports that strenuous, but but I did thoroughly test these Sports Clips by bending over, hopping up and down and generally moving my head a lot. They did not come loose from my ears.

I found another excellent use for them as well. When I have normal earbuds plugged in when I am baking bread or other dishes that get my hands very messy, all too frequently non-clip earbuds begin to slip out of my ears. Its a real pain to have to wash sticky dough off my hands and dry them before I can stuff the loose earbuds back into my ears. I don't have that problem at all with these Sports Clips earbuds, and that's very convenient.

The one flaw with this product, at least it's a flaw to me, because it doesn't make any sense and is somewhat uncomfortable, is the way the cord is designed. It is not coequal in length on both sides. One side is about four times longer than the other. There also isn't any sliding plastic piece that allows you to adjust the length of the splitting of the cord so that the user can adjust how wide it gaps over one's throat and chest, which would allow the user to opt, as desired, to even tighten it right up under the chin.

Other than those issues, this is an excellent product.
text_fidelity_b: JVC HAECX20B Sports Clip Inner Ear Headphones, Black

text_fidelity_a:
ContourROAM Hands-free HD Camcorder Picked up a couple of these when Amazon had them on sale for half price. Had to return one because it was out of focus; Amazon processed the return quickly and the replacement works great.

Very pleased with the image quality of these cameras in the 1080p mode (which I always use). The video quality is sharp and colorful. Make sure you use the camera software to set the image quality to the highest level for best results.

Sound quality is a mixed bag. This camera uses noise reduction to reduce wind noise (which is a big problem with older Contour cameras at even moderate bicycling speeds), but the noise reduction also severely muffles your voice if you are trying to narrate a video while filming.

The camera controls are very easy to use, which is an improvement over earlier Contour cameras. The instant-on feature works great if you're filming only pieces of your event. I get about 3 hours of video from one battery charge. That also seems to be the amount of video that fits on a 32GB microSD card. If your event is longer than 3 hours, use the instant-on/instant-off feature to switch the camera on for just the important parts. The instant-on feature is a nice improvement over earlier Contour cameras that are difficult to turn on when you are moving.

Contour cameras seem to go on sale more often than GoPro. If you can catch it at a good sale price, I think Contour is a much better value than GoPro.
text_fidelity_b: ContourROAM Hands-free HD Camcorder

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Paperwhite 3G, 6" High Resolution Display with Built-in Light, Free 3G + Wi-Fi - Includes Special Offers [Previous Generation - 5th] My title pretty much sums it up - I love the Kindle Paperwhite! I am a big reader, but I resisted the e-reader obsession until December 2010 when I gave into a Nook. Back then I decided on a Nook because the Kindle did not allow you to borrow books from the library, which was a deal breaker for me.

Fast-forward two and a half years... My Nook was getting older and the discrepancy between prices and availability of e-books between Amazon and Barnes & Noble was becoming increasingly clearer. Also, I love Amazon as a general rule, and order from them pretty heavily for a variety of items, so it made sense to switch over. After brief research, I stumbled upon the Kindle Paperwhite. It met all of my requirements - a dedicated e-reader (no tablet for me, thanks), with a built in light. Yippee! My hubby and puppy (okay, just the hubby) purchased the Kindle Paperwhite for my birthday at the end of August and it was love at first sight. It is unreasonable to compare the Kindle Paperwhite to my old Nook, so I won't. I can freely admit that most of my love comes from the new technology and association with Amazon. I love the light. It is awesome to not have to use a clip on light at night. They are usually terrible and not evenly spaced. The light makes reading at night a breeze. Plus, it is a perfect light, so it really is like reading a book and not like reading on a backlit screen (a la the iPhone or iPad). I love the ease of purchasing books from Amazon, and I love their prices and special deals. But, most of all, I love checking out library books! The very thing that turned me away from the Kindle initially is now the best. There is no need to connect my Kindle to a laptop to download a book. Yay! I can just wirelessly send a book to my Kindle, the same as purchasing one. You must be a wireless network (not 3G), but that my dear friends is a tiny issue. Overall, I love my Kindle Paperwhite and I cannot think of one single thing to make it better! Love it.

Helpful tips - 3G or not? I love the 3G, but it's not a necessity if you have wide access to wireless. I would definitely say to go for the ads, however. They are entirely inoffensive and unobtrusive. They only come up when your Kindle is asleep. Save the $20 and buy yourself a few books!
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Paperwhite 3G, 6" High Resolution Display with Built-in Light, Free 3G + Wi-Fi - Includes Special Offers [Previous Generation - 5th]

text_fidelity_a:
B-Land 10" Ring Light with Tripod Stand & 3 Phone Holders & Flexible Clip Microphone Holder for Multicam Live Stream, LED YouTube Lighting Kit Photo Light for Videos & Photography I am best described as a skilled amateur when it comes to photography and I am always looking for ways to get better and to build my knowledge and ability. I am not a professional by any means, but I know a lot more than the average selfie-taker. I have wanted a ring light for a little while and I was delighted to have the chance to get to use this one. It does work, in the right circumstances, but it is definitely aimed at the base consumer market and is priced accordingly.

Thought it can be used as part of a professional set-up, it is designed and marketed as a consumer-grade unit. There are a number of obvious design decisions that make this more than just a little apparent. The tripod is good, but the mounts are designed for smartphones and will not work for DSLR cameras, mirrorless cameras or video cameras. That’s ok, as it is clearly marketed that way. The unit uses a USB power source which is an important point – the light itself isn’t especially bright like one that uses a normal AC power source. To be effective, the light needs to be fairly close to the subject. If a dim directional light is needed, a regular desk lamp is more than adequate in most cases. The upshot is that using USB power makes it much more portable for travel (more on that in a moment).

The remote allows for making a few adjustments to the light itself. There are three color modes and ten brightness modes, all of which can be (rather, must be) set through the remote. The adjustments are sufficient for this grade of light, though I would have found more colors and a more smooth graduation in brightness to be more useful. That’s more of a nitpick than a criticism considering the price point.

Build-wise, this unit is acceptable. It should hold up well enough in the studio or home office. What is lacking is a carry case to protect it when travelling. Considering the target audience (social media producers), this is an oversight that I think is important. To transport this light, it should be well secured and the only recourse as sold is to put it back in the original box, and that’s just unwieldy. Plan accordingly if you choose to transport this light.

This is an adequate unit for its target audience but will leave the aspiring professional underwhelmed. If you are looking for something that will work sufficiently for making posts to social media this is a reasonable unit; if you need a serious ring light for photography, consider other options. The main problem with this light is the fact that it is designed for portability but comes with no carrying case; keep this in mind.
text_fidelity_b: B-Land 10" Ring Light with Tripod Stand & 3 Phone Holders & Flexible Clip Microphone Holder for Multicam Live Stream, LED YouTube Lighting Kit Photo Light for Videos & Photography

text_fidelity_a: Amazon Basics HDMI to RCA Converter We have a minivan with a DVD entertainment system pre-installed. It predates the HDMI standard, so there are just RCA analog inputs in the back of the van. Since DVDs are pretty much obsolete, using this adapter we are able to plug in a laptop, raspberry pi or other digital video player to the car's system. I like that it is powered by USB, it is a convenient source of power especially when you don't have access to outlets (like in a car!). But you have to be careful about ground loop feedback. When powering it off a laptop, and the laptop is charging in the car, it can create either an audible hum and/or visual static distortion pattern on the video feed. This is common in DC circuits that share ground when working with analog equipment, unfortunately. I'm not sure if there's much that can be done about it other than try to run off batteries as often as possible (with this converter attached to a USB battery bank, the laptop on its own power, and the car running its own 12v DC). I have an older similar product looks almost identical that does the same thing so I'm guessing that's just a side effect of working with RCA inputs instead of digital ones.
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Basics HDMI to RCA Converter

text_fidelity_a:
Acer Aspire R 15 2-in-1 Laptop, 15.6" Full HD Touch, 7th Gen Intel Core i7, GeForce 940MX, 12GB DDR4, 256GB SSD, R5-571TG-7229 This will be a fairly detailed and honest review.

1. Who is this for?
This computer is what I would consider a gateway computer. Those who are looking at upgrading a fairly old or not so powerful laptop and are looking to do a little more productivity, this is a great option.

2. What do you get?
Well you can probably read the description, however it's worth noting. You get an Intel i7 7500u CPU (dual core with 4 threads) 12gb DDR4 RAM, Nvidia 940mx GPU, a 256gb SSD, 15.6" 1080p screen, fingerprint reader, and a backlit keyboard.

The reason I mention all of the feautures is because you would be hardpressed to find another laptop with these features for the same price. To my knowledge there is not laptop on the market for $800 with an i7, dedicated graphics, 12gb of RAM and an SSD. This is really one of the best values on the market right now.

With all of that said, this isn't for everyone. If you want to do extensive gaming, this is not for you. Can it game? Yes, light gaming can be achieved, however it isn't marketed as a gaming laptop. Is this for someone who wants to do editing (video, audio, photos)? Yes, again light editing can be achieved.

What blew me away with this computer is the speakers! They are fantastic! I usually use headphones and would consider myself somewhat picky with sound, and for laptop speakers these are really something great.

This computer is really a middle of the pack all arounders dream. If you dabble in a little of this and a little of that but don't do anything professionally or extremely serious, this is really all you need.

Also, everyone's experience is different. Some hate loud fans, and if this is pushed the fans will be audible. Some don't like that the backlit keyboard times out after 30 seconds of no use. These things really don't bother me.

Lastly, the versatility of this laptop is really great. I've bought tablets and sold them because I couldn't justify having a laptop and tablet, then bought tablets again because I missed the things I could do with them that I was missing on a laptop. This solved all of those issues except size. It's pretty big, which for some is a plus others its not.

Overall, if you are looking at upgrading and don't want to spend $1,200-2,000 on a flagship model laptop this is a great option! I can't recommend this enough.
text_fidelity_b: Acer Aspire R 15 2-in-1 Laptop, 15.6" Full HD Touch, 7th Gen Intel Core i7, GeForce 940MX, 12GB DDR4, 256GB SSD, R5-571TG-7229

Portable Pocket WOWOTO Projector Android Mini Smart LED DLP Projector I was actually really shocked at how great this little portable speaker is. My cell phone found it in seconds, and in less than a minute I was listening to music from my cell phone, only out of this little speaker, it actually sounded great. In fact, the bass was so effective out of this thing that some of my favorite songs made it dance around the table.

You can actually control the music from your cell phone from the speaker itself. It has a pause/play button, forward and back, and volume controls. text_fidelity_a:
LotFancy Laptop Cooler Cooling Pad with 5 Quiet Fans for 12-17" Notebook, Dual USB Ports A good laptop chiller pad becomes important when you run a lot of graphics-intensive games or if you are doing anything requiring the CPU to run a heavy load. Heat is the enemy of a computer system and the fastest way to a dead laptop is to not deal with heat issues when there’s a problem. I had a chill pad some time ago and it was sub-par. This one by LotFancy is much better and it does a good job.

First off, this is a big chill pad, the same basic dimensions as my laptop but much thicker. I have a 15.6" laptop and this pad is almost a perfect and exact fit, with only a narrow area in the back that extends past the end of the laptop. If you want a small and petite chill pad, this is not the one you want. It does incline too with a metal bar and slots in the case so that the laptop can be angled up. This actually is good for exposing it to even more air.

This chill pad connects to a USB port so it can either be plugged into a port on the computer or into a hub. There are two ports on it and both seem to be the same in terms of how the pad operates. That is, the pad operates at the same speed regardless of which port is used. There are also two buttons on the pad for turning it on. One turns on the larger fan in the middle, and the other turns on all the other fans. Two green LEDs next to those buttons indicate that the pad is powered on and working.

This pad moves a lot of air and it does a good job of cooling the laptop. But, it does so very quietly which is a huge plus. I have it set up in my home office and the pad makes about as much noise as a desktop computer, maybe a little less. The sound it makes is a gentle hum.

When powered on each fan has a bright blue LED in it. While they look cool when there’s no laptop on the pad, they’re all but invisible when the laptop is sitting on top. There isn’t even much of a glow coming from the pad. I turned on the pad, turned out all of the lights and the glow from the laptop screen was enough to overpower any light that might have come from the pad. Except for the low hum I wouldn’t know it was even turned on.

This is a good chill pad. It works quietly and it moves a lot of air. Compared to other chill pads I have used this one is very good and I am happy to recommend it.

Disclaimer: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at no cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.
text_fidelity_b: LotFancy Laptop Cooler Cooling Pad with 5 Quiet Fans for 12-17" Notebook, Dual USB Ports

IFOOTAGE On-Camera Video Light, RGB Led light for Photography, APP Control/Keyframes, CRI 95+/2700-10000K, 2000mAh/Type C Charging, Mobile Video Cconference Light, Multiple Mounting Methods, C4/Yellow I'm impressed. This little guy is strong and bright! I've tried several lights, including handheld (like this), panel lights, ring lights, etc., and I have been very impressed with this one.

Before I dive into the good, let me discuss the bad: the iPhone app. I'm all for having an app to control the light and I totally understand why it's necessary. HOWEVER, this app REQUIRES that you sign up with an email and password. While there might be benefits to this (like accessing presets/settings across devices); I didn't check. Registering an account should 100% be optional. There is no reason to require me to register with my email + password so I can control this light via Bluetooth. As an aside, according to the Apple App Store, the developer does not collect any data from your phone (see pic); this is the reason I did not deduct a star for this.

My second gripe with the app, is that the it is a little rudimentary. Not particularly polished; and a little buggy at times (e.g. I couldn't get effects to kick in after selecting them on the app (I'd have to do it multiple times before the light would react), the light wouldn't always connect on the first try, etc. This was not the norm, but it happened a few times during my testing.

Now onto the good: First and foremost, it is BRIGHT. Brighter than similarly-sized lights. Physically, it feels well-designed. It has a 2000 mAh battery (I expected 1000 mAh). It is intuitive to operate and you can use it without the app if necessary (setting color temp, intensity, etc. No effects). There is a USB-C port for charging and a small display on the top, which shows battery %, time remaining (!), and color settings.

The soft cover on the front is attached magnetically, and can be attached to the back when you take it off (!); a wonderful design touch that is much appreciated. The light can also be affixed to metal surfaces via the magnet in the back.

The app, while barebones, provides a lot of functionality. There are many effects to choose from, and even a "music" mode in which the light will pulse to the beat of music picked up by your iPhone (or whatever device you are running the app on).

Overall, I have been really pleased with this light.
text_fidelity_b: IFOOTAGE On-Camera Video Light, RGB Led light for Photography, APP Control/Keyframes, CRI 95+/2700-10000K, 2000mAh/Type C Charging, Mobile Video Cconference Light, Multiple Mounting Methods, C4/Yellow

text_fidelity_a:
Sony ICFC218 Dream Machine Clock Radio (Black) This is not a bad clock radio for the price I paid. It's not a great one either, but it fit the profile of what I wanted with one exception, which I'll get to in a bit.

First off, it's smallish, which is a blessing on a crowded nightstand. The display seems fine to me, neither too bright, nor too dim. It's easy to program, thank goodness. I've had a lot of electronics that require three hands, and a stopwatch to be properly programmed. The ICF-C218 has a button or a dial for each function. Just follow the instructions and you'll be fine. It's a bit hard to see the radio dial unless you pick it up, but that's a minor thing for someone like me, who pretty much keeps it on one station. It's not programmable; you have to change the station with a tuning dial. However the reception is excellent, even without an external antenna.

My quibble, and it's a relatively small one, is that the sound is tinny. I don't expect a lot out of a small radio like this, but I have a Sangean which is even smaller, and the sound is much better. It's not a deal-breaker, I got what I wanted in every other respect.

Bottom line: Good price point for a basic clock radio with excellent reception, and so-so sound.
text_fidelity_b: Sony ICFC218 Dream Machine Clock Radio (Black)
