text_fidelity_a:
APC Power Strip with USB Charging Ports, Surge Protector P8U2, 2630 Joules, Flat Plug, 8 Outlets More electronics in the home means a need for more outlets. An ordinary extension cord will do the trick, but if you want something that looks nicer, has more functionality, and protects against power surges than one good option is the APC P11U2 APC Surge Arrest.

This surge protection device is great for those who need extra outlets for plugging in electronics and other things. It has eleven sockets plus 2 USB ports for a total of 13 places to plug things in and keep them running. An indicator light will tell you if there is an overload, which is highly possible when there are so any plugs. We don’t have this problem because we use this on our kid’s tech table. It allows them to plug in their cell phones, tablets, kindles, and other items- all which use minimal power- and get everything charged all at once without them fighting over limited outlet availability.

Each of the outlets on this surge protector has a safety closure, which is good for keeping out unwanted items. This can be useful if you have young children- wouldn’t want junior sticking a paper clip or other item inside one of the sockets. And a light glows to indicate that the surge protection is working as it should.

If I could change one thing about this, it would be the length of the cord. It would be better if it was just a little longer because it would be capable of reaching further. But other than that, this surge protector has worked just fine for my needs. It has ample space to plug in and charge all of our household electronics, keeping them ready for use and protecting against power spikes in the process.
text_fidelity_b: APC Power Strip with USB Charging Ports, Surge Protector P8U2, 2630 Joules, Flat Plug, 8 Outlets

text_fidelity_a:
Pangea Audio Vulcan TT Turntable Stand with Vinyl Record Storage - Black Some appear to have had some difficulty or confusion with assembly, but I did it solo fairly quickly with no issues and found the instructions very clear. No tools were needed and all of the pieces went on smoothly. The direction sheet clearly shows and lists what pieces to use. I guess some didn’t see that one of the shelf sections is thicker. The stand appears quite sturdy and stable. Yes, the only real issue is if you’re using the discs at the feet. I guess the bare, spike type feet ends are supposed to be for thick carpet. Like many I had mine on wood/laminate flooring and so need the small discs as the spike tips will surely scratch it up. This isn’t really a problem per se, but it is quite finicky and it the only part of the operation my wife had to assist with. It definitely would’ve been nice if they’d just included both a spike and attached foot type tips with the stand especially at this price. I included two pics with this review that I took while in the process of getting it and components situated. The stand easily fits my vintage Sansui 661 receiver on the middle shelf and Audio Technica LP120 turntable on the top. I hope both this review and photos showing it with the perspective of having components on it help.

Edit: So, yea, I did dock a star due to the feet issue. As I noted they are finicky, but can quickly get frustrating. While I had to move the stand around getting my stereo stuff sorted the small discs constantly came off and you just really can’t put them back in solo. They will and did put small indentations on my floor with the discs off. My solution was to pick up a 4 pack of 1” sliders from WM that are plastic on the bottom with an adhesive disc on the top. I then stuck the small metal discs from the stand on the slider. Once my wife helped me place the discs back on the legs it could then slide pretty freely and they stayed on. It’s a shame they didn’t include a normal leg along with the pins. I still like the stand quite a bit, but I’d warn people with mobility issues against this one even as nice as it is.
text_fidelity_b: Pangea Audio Vulcan TT Turntable Stand with Vinyl Record Storage - Black

text_fidelity_a:
Echo Show - 1st Generation Black Not liking this very much at all. I never owned a echo or anything like this. I got a deal on it for $159. I thought I would use it more. Because YouTube isn’t part of it anymore (and I knew that before buying it )but figured there would be other videos to watch. I do a lot of DIY projects. This doesn’t bring up anything I ask it. I’ll ask Alexa please show me cocoa butter Lotion, chapstick,or body wash recipes,whatever I plan on making and so forth but it will bring up baking recipes for cookies or other things instead. I can get everything on my iPhone so I really don’t even need this for that. I figured it be easier instead of getting my phone all gross while making my products.
I used it a few times to call my sister because she has one too. I also used it for the drop in for when I’m away to check on my house and my cats. Though the noise it makes scares them. while my sister was taking care of my house while I was a way last week, when I called her on it, she said my voice was distorted and it was making a weird high pitch sound. I couldn’t hear it on my end though. So maybe something is wrong with it? Since I’m not getting much use out of it as I thought I would, I may end up returning it. It’s expensive to just sit on my table or counter collecting dust. The commercials made it look really neat and useful. Also, everything else extra for it like the outlets to turn lights on and the cameras are pretty expensive. I don’t know if I’ll ever be able to afford to buy them in the future. I guess I should’ve done more research before purchasing. I got it on Inpulse bc the price was cheaper and the sale wasn’t gonna last much longer that day, plus I was able to set up a payment plan which made it much more affordable. I’ll have to think about it some more to see if I really want to keep it. As of now, it’s pretty useless. The camera part to check in on my house, I can do with my tablet and a free app. So that will cost me nothing.
text_fidelity_b: Echo Show - 1st Generation Black

Sony X80J 50 Inch TV: 4K Ultra HD LED Smart Google TV with Dolby Vision HDR and Alexa Compatibility KD50X80J- 2021 Model Beautiful bright, sharp, vivid picture from this tv! Has very deep nice blacks which is something I always look for. Google setup on this is easy and the A frame legs are easy to put on. Tv was pretty easy to wall mount and looks beautiful on the wall!

The sound is really good, I don't even need to use a soundbar with this tv! I love the acoustic auto calibration- you sit on the couch and start it- it blasts sound in several directions thru the speakers and the mic on your remote picks it up and adjusts the sound based on where you're sitting and what kind of room you're in. Another amazing sound feature is the bluetooth they added in on this one, you can use bluetooth headphones with this!

The motion on it is pretty decent, it has enhanced motion features you can turn on for say sports and gaming but for regular tv watching, you won't want them on. This tv can adjust the brightness based on the lighting in the room which is impressive.

Tv switches between apps and thru the apps extremely smoothly! Overall I think this is an amazing tv packed in at a really modest price that won't send you to the poor house! If you have a higher budget and want top of the line, check out Sony's 90J series which is a step up from the 80J. But on a budget- this tv will certainly make you happy, it's an amazing machine!

One day it just stopped charging. I had read dozens of books on there, and had the wifi plus 3g version which was very convenient.

I occasionally read now on the Kindle app on my computer, as I have about 97 books in my library, with probably 15-20 still unread. I noticed on Amazon that there was a promotion...Kindles on sale for Prime members. I thought, you know, it would be nice to read those books I've put off reading because it's just not the same on my computer or phone...I think I'll get another Kindle. I researched reviews for a little while, and decided all I needed was the Paperwhite with Wi-fi. The additional cost for 3G was just not worth it to me...sure, I'd used it before when traveling with my old Kindle to buy a few books, but with a little planning I could've purchased and downloaded the books beforehand. Also, some of the reviews of the higher end Kindles did not impress me.

Anyway, I received the Kindle earlier today. It came almost fully charged, and was so easy to set up. And within minutes had books from my Kindle library loaded! I've been reading for 2 hours straight and so far I love it. I am using it on maximum brightness, sure it may take more frequent charging, but I really love how bright it is and the contrast of the words on the page. I also bought a cover for it and find it is easier to hold IMO. Pages turned with a simple finger swipe.

Hopefully this will last a very long time! I've got so many books I want to read!

Acer Chromebook 15 CB3-532-C4ZZ, Celeron N3060, 15.6" HD, 4GB LPDDR3, 32GB Storage, Google Chrome Electronics are a fact of life and most families have multiple electronic devices to get through their day. My family of four has four cell phones, about six different pcs, laptops, and tablets, and three printers. Now, we also have our first ever Chromebook thanks to this Amazon product.

Chromebooks, I quickly learned, differ from the usual windows or apple laptop in several important ways and chief among them is the limit on the number of things you can download. If you have specific games and other things you want to download, they may not work. I already knew this going in but I can tell from reading other reviews that some people were not aware that it worked this way and they now have a device with limited usefulness.

Once you accept the Acer Chromebook for what it is, you will find that it does serve as a handy device. It’s excellent for browsing the internet, creating google docs, using google apps, and pretty much doing all things google. I am already a google chrome user when I go online and I already use many apps from the google play, so what this Chromebook offers is compatible with my needs.

Looking at other specifics of this Acer Chromebook, it is about the same size as my old laptop, at least in terms of the screen size. The image is good, although I have seen other laptops/tablets with more pixels and sharper images. Still, it should be sufficient for most needs, and it has a good deal to offer for the price. I have noticed that the charge doesn’t hold as long as the manufacturer claims and the bottom of the Chromebook does feel hot a little sooner than with others. But the Acer Chromebook is still functional and it performs well enough for my needs.

Electronics are a fact of life and as much as we try to limit their use, they are here to stay. Since we have to have them and use them, it makes sense to get the electronics that best suit our needs for a fair price and this Acer Chromebook does exactly that. It does have its limits and it cannot do everything that a windows or apple laptop can do, but as long as you know the limitations before you purchase, you should be fine.
text_fidelity_b: Acer Chromebook 15 CB3-532-C4ZZ, Celeron N3060, 15.6" HD, 4GB LPDDR3, 32GB Storage, Google Chrome
